notes.title: ‘83 Development Update - Growing the Team
notes.notes:
Soldiers!

We would like to say a massive thank you to everyone for your support and feedback since we released our re-announcement trailer, the enthusiasm for ‘83 and what we are building has been brilliant and we’re very excited to share more with you on the road to launch. 

Since the announcement, the ‘83 team has been growing rapidly across development, community, cinematics and marketing, and we plan to share development progress here showcasing updates across different maps, weapons, gameplay mechanics and what to expect when it comes to ‘accessible realism’ in ‘83. 

Development update - April 2025

Our level design team has officially begun crafting brand new environments, expanding the future battlegrounds you'll explore. While we can't reveal specifics just yet, the process of bringing these new locations from concept to reality is well underway and incredibly exciting for us.
 
Simultaneously, we've been dedicating significant effort to refining the core experience. This includes ongoing network optimization work aimed at ensuring smooth, stable online gameplay. Our animation department has also been busy, focusing on enhancing the feel and responsiveness of weapon handling to make those in-game moments even more immersive.
 
Underpinning all of this is our continued work with Unreal Engine 5. We're constantly striving to harness the power of UE5 to deliver the best possible visual fidelity and performance for '83.
It's been a productive period, and the positive energy in the studio is palpable.

Weapons showcase 

The team has also been busy working on a range of different weapons that players can expect to get their hands on when we launch in Early Access this year including the RPG-7, AKS-74U and AK-74, we’re pleased to share some screenshots of these below (with much more to come in future trailers)

notes.title: '83 Development Update – January 2025
notes.notes:
Dear ‘83 Community!

We’re excited to bring you our first development update of the new year.

Thanks to the feedback from the 8 playtests we’ve held so far, we’ve been able to make significant strides in server performance. Our code team "assaulted" these challenges head-on, and we’re now able to support sufficient player counts to start showing the fun aspects of the game to testers!

Overall, these tests have been invaluable in helping us debug several critical issues, and it's been great to see players not just fill, and stress test the servers, but also enjoy the game as it’s meant to be played with 75 players running! 

Production Goals for January and February
Looking ahead, we’re now turning our focus towards weapons and animations. This is no small task, as we've essentially had to recreate the animation framework from the ground up. 

Without being too specific (to manage expectations), we also want to give you a look at our overarching production plan for the next two months. Here’s what the team is focused on delivering:

January:

 Rollout of an all-new animation framework
 Significant progress on weapons systems

February:

 Continued optimization along with key additions and tweaks to core gameplay systems
 Full Integration of Unreal Engine 5 features like Nanite and Virtual Shadow Maps for visually stunning environments with a manageable GPU load
 Deeper exploration of UE5's IRIS networking architecture, which we aim to leverage for smoother, large-scale multiplayer performance

The Path to Our Vertical Slice
By the end of February, we’re aiming to achieve a critical milestone of the ’83 project: the vertical slice build. We’ve had many of you asking what specifically that means – roughly, this is the gist of it:

[olist]
 "Show the Fun in ‘83": A showcase of one example map where core gameplay loop of ’83 shows its main fun element
 Core Gameplay Systems: Demonstrate most of the core systems that define the ‘83 experience
 Graphics Optimizations: We’re aiming to implement Nanites and Virtual Shadow Maps to deliver the best possible visuals along with scalable performance
 Server Stability: Further optimize the game to support for 80-player servers without server CPU or network hiccups
 Gather more HW spec data: Collection of data to define accurate minimum and recommended system requirements.
[/olist]
Closing Thoughts
The year is off to a great start, and we’d like to thank all of you for your continued support and enthusiasm. Your feedback and participation in playtests have helped shape the game into what it is today, and we can’t wait to show you what we’ve been building as we move closer to our vertical slice goals.

We’re also excited to report that we’re putting additional focus on the marketing side of things – and we want to deliver a proper update to our Steam page in January, including new screenshots and a trailer. 

Stay tuned for more updates!

The 83 Development Team

notes.title: '83 Development Update: now Improving Net Code to Allow Playtesting!
notes.notes:
Dear community,

We're excited to update you on '83's development journey. Our team is working hard on our current primary objective: to get a stable build ready for closed community playtests, with the main hurdle so far being sub-par network performance. 

Fortunately, running the game on a powerful bare metal Windows server (as opposed to the standard, more cost effective cloud-powered virtual machine we aim to use) offers acceptable performance and enables us to begin some level of testing – as we proved in a short, closed test earlier this weekend.

Our progress in net code optimization is now driven by a talented duo of experienced programmers, which marks a significant improvement from a few months ago when we solely relied on volunteers. The development ultimately moved from a slow crawl to a steady jog and we are continuously gaining momentum!

Thank you for your ongoing support and patience as we continue to bring '83 to life. Your feedback is invaluable, so stay tuned for more updates!

o7
